infoDescription: Ornitho2eBird converts exports from ornitho, Observation and BirdLasser into eBird-ready checklists.
infoHowItWorksIntro: eBird only collects lists, so all imported observations must be converted to eBird checklists. The tool handles imported lists and casual observations differently.
infoHowItWorksChecklistIntro: Collecting data as lists on ornitho (complete or not) makes conversion to eBird much easier and is therefore strongly recommended.
infoHowItWorksChecklistPointOne: Easy conversion into eBird checklists because almost all metadata is already available.
infoHowItWorksChecklistPointTwo: Using the track in Naturalist is strongly recommended so checklist distance can be carried over automatically. Without distance, checklists become historical in eBird.
infoHowItWorksChecklistPointThree: Number of observers is not recorded in ornitho, so the app uses the default value defined in Settings.
infoHowItWorksChecklistPointFour: The app assumes that if you submitted a list, birding was the primary purpose.
infoHowItWorksSightingsIntro: Casual observations need to be aggregated into checklists before export.
infoHowItWorksSightingsPointOne: The app uses an automatic aggregation based on time and distance parameters (see below for details).
infoHowItWorksSightingsPointThree: Birding is not assumed to be the [primary purpose] for these checklists, so they are not marked as primary purpose by default.
infoHowItWorksSightingsPointFour: These checklists are not considered [complete] by default.
infoAutoAssignTitle: How does the aggregation of casual observation work?
infoAutoAssignIntro: The tool automatically groups casual observations into new checklists based on distance and time parameters (see settings).
infoAutoAssignPointTwo: The first casual observation becomes the seed of a new checklist. Later casual observations are added to that checklist when they occur on the same calendar day and fall within both the distance and duration thresholds of at least one observation already in the checklist. Otherwise, they start a new checklist. Aggregation never spans midnight.
infoAutoAssignPointThree: Nearby observations can form chains beyond the overall time or distance limit. If a later observation matches two existing checklists, it joins one; the checklists are not merged.
infoAutoAssignPointFour: Aggregation creates new checklists only. It does not add casual observations to existing checklists.
infoAutoAssignPointFive: If no time is available, the casual observation is treated as 00:00. With the default 24-hour duration threshold, same-day aggregation is therefore driven mainly by distance.
infoAutoAssignPointSix: The duration and distance thresholds can be adjusted in Settings.
infoCustomizeTitle: How to manually customize your checklist?
infoCustomizeBody: Turn on Customized mode in Settings to manually assign casual observations to checklists and edit checklist metadata before export, including primary purpose, protocol, date, time, duration, distance, observers, location and checklist comments.
infoCustomizeSpeciesComments: You can also modify species comments. Use the template settings to decide what information is added to each eBird species comment, such as count, time, links to the source observation, map links and original notes.
faqDuplicatesQuestion: How do I avoid importing the same observations twice?
faqDuplicatesAnswer: eBird does not check whether observations are already in your account, so importing them twice creates duplicate checklists. Before each import, check [your eBird checklists] for observations you already entered or imported. Import each period only once and note the last date you imported.
faqLargeImportsQuestion: I want to import many years of observations. What should I know?
faqLargeImportsAnswer: Large imports, especially of older observations, mean a lot of work for the volunteers who review eBird records in your region. Contact them before you start (through [eBird's help form] if you don't know who they are), and try a small import first.
faqNotForEbirdQuestion: Which observations should not go to eBird?
faqNotForEbirdAnswer: eBird checklists contain only live birds that you detected yourself during the checklist. Leave out dead birds, birds reported to you by others and recordings from automatic sound recorders (NocMig), which eBird handles separately. See [eBird best practices].
faqSpeciesMatchingQuestion: eBird asks me to match some species. Is that normal?
faqSpeciesMatchingAnswer: Yes, for Rock Pigeon and Common Snipe, whose scientific names eBird's import does not recognise, and for species the app could not link to eBird (the export page lists them). Choose the right species once on eBird's Fix species page: eBird remembers your choice for later imports, so choose carefully. Right after eBird's yearly taxonomy update (usually in October), a few more species may need matching until the app is updated.
faqHotspotsQuestion: How do I link a checklist to an eBird hotspot?
faqHotspotsAnswer: Select the hotspot on the map in Customized mode and use it as the checklist location. The CSV exports its eBird location ID so eBird can match it directly. A name and coordinates alone may create a personal location. For checklists already imported, [merge the location with the hotspot]: all its checklists then move to the hotspot. If you rename or move the location afterward, select the hotspot again to restore the link.
faqProcessingQuestion: My import has been processing for days.
faqProcessingAnswer: eBird can take several days, sometimes up to a week, to process an import. This is normal and cannot be sped up. You can follow it on [My Imports].
faqMistakesQuestion: I made a mistake in an import. How do I fix it?
faqMistakesAnswer: It is usually easiest to delete the import on [My Imports], fix the problem in ornitho2eBird and import a new file, rather than editing each checklist in eBird.
faqRaritiesQuestion: Do I need to document rare species?
faqRaritiesAnswer: Yes. Imports skip eBird's request for details on unusual sightings, so add photos or a description in eBird for rarities and unusually high counts. Keep the source link in species comments (on by default): it lets reviewers check the original observation.
faqDistanceQuestion: Why are distances in miles in the CSV?
faqDistanceAnswer: The app shows kilometres, but eBird's import format requires miles. eBird then shows distances in the units of your account.
faqMore: Another question or a problem? [Open an issue on GitHub] with your source website, what you did and what went wrong.

assignmentIntro: Casual observations have been automatically aggregated to checklists. Use this map to manually override those assignments: create a new checklist by drawing a rectangle over all observations; select an existing checklist and draw a rectangle to assign observations to it; choose "0. Non-assigned" to remove observations from a checklist. Casual observations left under "0. Non-assigned" will not be exported.

Aggregation creates new checklists only; it does not add observations to existing checklists.

analyticsSummary: May we use optional cookies to learn how people use the tool? Usage statistics help us improve importing, checklist review and exporting.
analyticsNotice: With your permission, Google receives visit and interaction data, including the source website you select, your interface language, mode, and use of checklist and map tools. We do not send file names, observation data, coordinates, comments, tokens, searches or full URLs in our events. Google also processes technical information such as your IP address and browser information, and may process data outside your country. Advertising consent stays denied and Google Signals and ad personalisation are disabled in this app. Analytics cookies and your saved choice expire after six months. You can change your choice here or through Privacy & cookies in the footer or Settings. Rejecting stops measurement and removes this app’s Analytics cookies without discarding your import. Language and app settings are stored separately to make the tool work. Google Analytics retains event data for two months and user data for fourteen months; new activity restarts the user-data retention period. Export events also record the species-comment option used and whether the CSV includes species comments, without their contents.
analyticsReassurance: Your observations and comment text are not collected. All features work without these cookies.
exportDateWarning: Checklist {name} contains a date mismatch or crosses midnight. All exported observations will use {date}. Review the dates; ordinary eBird checklists cover one calendar day.
exportExcludedWarning: {count} dead-bird or zero-count records are excluded from the CSV. Their original counts and comments remain available in the app.

splitDatesConfirm: Create one checklist per observation date? All records and comments are kept. Start time uses the first sighting on each day. Duration, distance and paths will be cleared because effort cannot be divided reliably; review them after splitting.
splitDatesUnavailable: Automatic splitting needs an exact date and time for every sighting, with sightings on more than one date. This checklist will remain together unless you edit it.
uniqueDistanceHelp: GPS estimates: stationary classification uses the widest separation among the central 95% of track points, ignoring isolated errors. A brief real excursion can also be ignored. Unique distance excludes closely overlapping segments; GPS drift and nearby paths can affect it. Review the track and adjust the distance if needed.
noEligibleRecords: No observations remain eligible for CSV export. Review the excluded records below.
